method_applied: anti-ai-slop-human-copy-filter: research first, context lock, rejected generic version, send/save/comment job before copy
superpowers:brainstorming spirit: interrogated the send trigger and compared several approaches before selecting candidates
astory source-winner loop: checked compatible winner-bank posts before fresh invention

local_performance_evidence.finding: A Story ideas should be ranked by shares per 1k reach and saves, not likes. DYJpjt9CQYY is the strongest cited send-behavior winner at 40.15 shares per 1k reach and 13.14 saves per 1k.
The top local winner used a direct send-to-person posture and emotionally specific partner behavior. It had 21,351 shares on 531,805 reach.
Ordinary-life-with-the-right-person framing travelled: 1,821 shares on 65,274 reach, 27.9 shares per 1k.
Specific ordinary details drove saves: 1,590 saves on 93,580 reach, 16.99 saves per 1k.

winner_bank_evidence.usable_engine: The familiar topic 'home is a person' has proven travel, but it is also the obvious generic trap.
Direct person-as-home captioning can pull tags and comments when it feels like a line someone can send.

winner_bank_evidence.metric_signal: 52,514 likes, 164 comments, 10-slide carousel, explicit direct-you/send mechanic
winner_bank_evidence.usable_engine: Small care phrases work as love because they let someone send an unsaid feeling without making a speech.
House-to-home transformation is proven, but the A Story version must avoid becoming a generic gratitude quote.

copy_contract_evidence.finding: Every line should feel like something someone could send; the copy should aim for 'I needed to say this' before 'this is a carousel.'
The old topic is 'home is a person'; the new reveal must be the physical emptiness of a place that has everything except the person.

evidence_ledger.evidence_gap: No live platform research was used. This pass relies on local A Story outcomes, the permissioned winner bank, and the run memory recall.
evidence_ledger.rejected_generic_version: Slide 1: the lyric. Slide 2: 'home is not a place, it is a person.' That version is true, dead, and too easy for any quote page.
evidence_ledger.named_send_trigger: Send this to the person you miss because saying 'I miss you' feels too small, but saying 'the whole place feels wrong without you' lands.

premise_lock.creator_setup_to_preserve: Slide 1 must use exactly: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera
premise_lock.slide_2_job: Turn the lyric into a simple note that carries both ache and comfort: the place has things, routines, maybe people, but the one real ghar-person is missing.
premise_lock.speaker: One partner speaking to the other as a private message, not as a public lesson about love.
premise_lock.receiver: The person whose presence changes a room from address to ghar.
premise_lock.human_situation: Someone is in a familiar place that should feel complete, but it does not feel like home until one specific person is there.
must_not_move_away_from: No added song lyrics beyond the creator-provided line
No generic 'home is a person' quote-card
locked_emotional_job: make someone send it to their person
make someone feel safe enough to come back tired, quiet, or imperfect
bait warm comments like 'this is us' or a tagged name
premise_lock.idea_stage_boundary: These are shareability directions only: no final story beats, no prompt writing, no image generation.

source_winner_basis.primary_basis: Use the winner-bank's proven 'home/person' travel, but repair the genericness by making slide 2 a private Aachu/Zuv message with lived absence and a sendable return line.

compatible_sources.what_stays: The familiar emotional truth: sometimes one person is the real home.
compatible_sources.what_changes: A Story version cannot stop at the slogan; it must show the emptiness caused by one specific absence.

compatible_sources.what_stays: The simple sendable grammar of naming one person as home.
compatible_sources.what_changes: Make it about Aachu/Zuv longing, not a general married-life quote.

compatible_sources.what_stays: Love expressed through small, direct care language.
compatible_sources.what_changes: The care phrase becomes 'come back as you are' rather than a list of domestic acts.

not_using_as_primary.reason: Solitude-as-home moves away from the creator's specific one-person ache.
House-to-home gratitude is compatible but risks becoming family/milestone content instead of this specific romantic absence.

candidates.title: Bas Aa Jaana
candidates.suggested_text_hook: Slide 1: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera. Slide 2 direction: sab kuch hai yahan. bas tum nahi ho. thak ke bhi aa jaana. yeh ghar tumhara hi hai.
candidates.one_line_concept: The lyric opens the ache; the payoff turns it into the safest possible invitation: come back imperfect, this place is still yours.
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1 keeps the creator's exact lyric as the stop-scroll ache.
Slide 2 turns the lyric into a private note: everything is here except you, and you do not need to arrive perfect to belong here.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A quiet frame where the place feels lived in but paused; the absence is readable through space, not through a decorative prop.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The emotional turn is not 'I miss you' but 'come back as you are; this home has kept your place.'
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Send trigger: for couples apart, late, fighting softly, or tired of pretending they are okay. Comment trigger: 'bas aa jaana' and tagged names.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It gives people a gentler way to say 'I need you here' without sounding needy or dramatic.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: The line invites direct tagging and small confession comments: 'this is us', 'come home', 'I am sending this to him.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: A soft chest-hit first, then immediate send to the person whose absence changes the room.
candidates.why_not_generic: It does not stop at 'home is a person.' It adds the riskier, more sendable detail: you can come back tired and still be wanted.

source_engine.source_type: source-preserving remix plus A Story performance memory

source_winners.engine_used: direct send-to-person framing beats like-only romance

source_engine.copy_status: creator-provided lyric preserved; slide 2 is an A Story original note, not more song lyric

novelty_model.new_reveal: The missing person does not just make the room empty; they are the person the room is saving space for.
novelty_model.viewer_outcome: The viewer can send a comforting invitation instead of a needy 'where are you?'
novelty_model.contrast_frame: Not address versus person; complete-looking place versus the one absence that makes it incomplete.
novelty_model.bullseye_proof: The payoff line creates a DM someone can send after missing their partner or after a hard day.

a_story_wrappers: Aachu/Zuv private note energy, not quote-card typography.
Restrained lived-home frame with negative space doing the emotional work.
The second slide feels like one partner speaking, not the brand explaining.

anti_slop_risk.risk: Could become a pretty quote about home if the comfort line gets over-polished.
anti_slop_risk.rejected_generic_version: Home is not a place, it is you.
anti_slop_risk.repair_rule: Keep the human phrase 'bas aa jaana' and the imperfect-return comfort.

failure_risks: AI_SLOP_COPY_DRIFT if the note becomes a moral about love
ORIGINAL_SETUP_DRIFT if slide 2 stops responding to the lyric
VISUAL_ONLY_MOOD_WORDS if the frame is only cozy/romantic instead of readable absence

candidates.title: Bas Tum Nahi Ho
candidates.suggested_text_hook: Slide 1: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera. Slide 2 direction: sab kuch hai yahan. bas tum nahi ho. isliye ghar bhi ghar nahi lagta.
candidates.one_line_concept: The place is not empty because nothing exists there; it is empty because the only person who makes it ghar is missing.
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1 gives the lyric as ache.
Slide 2 lands the blunt emotional proof: the house has everything except the person.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A room that should feel complete but feels too still; enough life to prove this is not poverty of objects, only absence of person.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The reader realizes the emptiness is not architectural. It is one-name specific.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Send trigger: the simplest 'I miss you' replacement. Comment trigger: people naming their person or saying 'ghar bhi ghar nahi lagta.'
candidates.why_people_may_share: It is painfully easy to send because it says the exact missing-person feeling without requiring a long message.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: The line gives people a safe way to admit dependence: 'same', 'this line', 'ghar is him/her.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Immediate recognition from long-distance couples and anyone sitting in a familiar place that feels wrong.
candidates.why_not_generic: It avoids the slogan and gives the viewer the specific contradiction: everything is present, but the place is still incomplete.

source_winners.engine_used: ordinary place/time becomes meaningful with the right person

source_engine.copy_status: creator-provided lyric preserved; payoff is original Hinglish note

novelty_model.new_reveal: The place is materially full but emotionally empty because one person is absent.
novelty_model.viewer_outcome: A sendable missing-you line that feels less dramatic than a confession.
novelty_model.bullseye_proof: The phrase 'bas tum nahi ho' is short enough to be a DM and specific enough to tag.

a_story_wrappers: Let Aachu/Zuv's absence be felt in the frame rather than explained.
Keep slide 2 as a private spoken line.
Use quiet domestic logic without making an object the premise.

anti_slop_risk.risk: The idea is close to the generic source phrase, so the final wrapper must prove 'bas tum nahi ho' through lived absence.
anti_slop_risk.rejected_generic_version: This house is empty without you because you are my home.
anti_slop_risk.repair_rule: Keep the contradiction: everything is here, only you are not.

failure_risks: GENERIC_IDEA if it becomes only 'home is you'
WEAK_PAYOFF if slide 2 repeats slide 1 without adding the full-house/empty-heart contrast
SHARE_TRIGGER_MISSING if the line becomes too polished to send

candidates.title: Tumhari Jagah
candidates.suggested_text_hook: Slide 1: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera. Slide 2 direction: ghar mein ek jagah aisi hai jo kisi aur se nahi bharni. woh tumhari hai.
candidates.one_line_concept: The home is not empty everywhere; it has one precise place that only this person can fill.
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 2 makes the ache specific: not loneliness, not decoration, one reserved emotional place.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: A still pause in the home with room for the missing person; not a melodramatic lonely pose.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The sendable comfort is 'your place is still yours.'
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Send trigger: for couples who want to reassure each other after distance or a rough patch. Comment trigger: 'meri jagah', 'saved this', tagged initials.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It lets someone say 'you are irreplaceable here' without sounding like a formal anniversary caption.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will tag their person because 'tumhari jagah' sounds like a private inside claim.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Less instant than candidate 1, but deeper saves from people who want a softer reassurance post.
candidates.why_not_generic: Instead of claiming a universal truth, it points to one exact unfilled place and lets the viewer feel it.

source_winners.engine_used: specific ordinary details create save behavior

novelty_model.new_reveal: The ache is not broad loneliness; it is one reserved space that refuses substitutes.
novelty_model.viewer_outcome: The receiver feels wanted without being idealized.
novelty_model.contrast_frame: A place that can be occupied by many people versus a place only one person fills.
novelty_model.bullseye_proof: The phrase gives commenters an easy handle: 'tumhari jagah.'

a_story_wrappers: Negative space as proof, not gimmick.
Aachu/Zuv implied through one reserved side/place rather than both forced into frame.
Private message tone with no public lesson.

anti_slop_risk.risk: Could become too poetic if 'place' turns abstract.
anti_slop_risk.rejected_generic_version: No one can take your place in my heart.
anti_slop_risk.repair_rule: Keep it grounded as ghar-space, not heart-space.

failure_risks: TOO_POLISHED if the reserved-place line becomes literary
VISUAL_ONLY_MOOD_WORDS if the scene does not make the reserved space readable
LOW_SCORE_NO_SELECTION if other agents need a sharper three-second hook

candidates.title: Address Nahi
candidates.suggested_text_hook: Slide 1: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera. Slide 2 direction: ghar mera address nahi hai. ghar woh feeling hai jo sirf tumhare aane se aati hai.
candidates.one_line_concept: It moves the lyric from a house metaphor to a body feeling: the address stays the same, but ghar only arrives with the person.
suggested_slide_arc: Slide 1 gives the line as ache.
Slide 2 reframes ghar as the feeling that arrives with one person.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: The first frame should feel like a known place waiting, not like a designed quote background.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The comfort is that home is not lost; it comes back when they do.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Send trigger: good for people who live away, shift cities, or feel safe only with one person. Comment trigger: 'address nahi', 'this is my person.'
candidates.why_people_may_share: It gives city/long-distance couples a clean way to say the place is secondary and the person is the real anchor.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People can tag their person with minimal context because the line explains itself quickly.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Broadly relatable and very easy to understand, though a little closer to known quote territory.
candidates.why_not_generic: The A Story wrapper must keep the lyric's emptiness first, then use address as a contrast, not as a clever slogan.

source_engine.copy_status: creator lyric preserved; payoff is original but adjacent to proven source language

novelty_model.new_reveal: The address can be correct and still not feel like ghar until one person enters it.
novelty_model.viewer_outcome: A broad sendable line for long-distance, moving, or waiting couples.
novelty_model.bullseye_proof: The phrase is instantly legible on slide 2, but needs visual specificity to avoid quote-card blandness.

a_story_wrappers: Use Aachu/Zuv's lived environment to avoid a poster-style address metaphor.
Keep the tone private and unslick.
Do not make maps, keys, signs, or address props the premise.

anti_slop_risk.risk: This is the most quote-page-adjacent candidate.
anti_slop_risk.rejected_generic_version: Home is not an address, it is a feeling.
anti_slop_risk.repair_rule: Only keep this if the scene and line stay tied to the creator's lyric and the person's arrival.

failure_risks: GENERIC_IDEA if address/feeling becomes the whole premise
AI_SLOP_COPY_DRIFT if it turns into motivational copy
SHARE_TRIGGER_MISSING if it sounds like a caption people admire but do not send

top_pick.title: Bas Aa Jaana
top_pick.why_this_wins: It has the cleanest send reason: it does not merely say 'you are home'; it gives the receiver somewhere to return. That is both ache and comfort in one swipe.
top_pick.three_second_hook: The creator's lyric catches the Ghar-memory audience; 'bas aa jaana' gives everyone else the DM reason.
top_pick.named_send_trigger: Send to the person you want home, especially if they are tired, late, distant, or emotionally hard to reach.
comment_bait: tagging the person whose place is still kept
top_pick.selection_note: Pick this if the room wants the most comfort. Pick candidate 02 if the room wants the sharpest ache.

engagement_rationale.share_logic: The strongest route is not a clever lyric translation. It is a message someone can forward because it says 'I need you here' without sounding demanding.
engagement_rationale.comment_logic: Warm comments will come from tags and tiny confessions, not debate. The candidate should invite 'come home', 'this is us', and name-tag comments.
engagement_rationale.save_logic: The post can save well if slide 2 becomes a line people want to keep for later, especially after distance, a hard day, or a quiet fight.
engagement_rationale.swipe_logic: Slide 1 has built-in curiosity because it is a known beloved line. Slide 2 must reward the swipe with a private note, not a paraphrase.
engagement_rationale.distribution_prediction: Best audience: long-distance couples, married/committed couples with routine separations, people who use Hindi/Hinglish emotional language, and viewers who save missing-you posts.

distribution_risks.risk: The theme is already widely proven, so the generic version will feel like a quote account.
distribution_risks.mitigation: Keep the second slide as a private spoken note with 'bas aa jaana' or 'bas tum nahi ho' specificity.

distribution_risks.risk: Using a song line may attract recognition but also raise expectation for more lyrics.
distribution_risks.mitigation: Do not add more song lyrics. Make slide 2 original A Story copy.

distribution_risks.risk: Too much Hinglish may reduce reach for non-Hindi viewers, but too little loses the creator's setup.
distribution_risks.mitigation: Keep the key feeling in simple Hinglish and make the visual emotion readable without translation.

distribution_risks.risk: Two slides can feel thin if slide 2 only explains slide 1.
distribution_risks.mitigation: Slide 2 must add a new emotional turn: return-as-you-are, everything-here-except-you, or your-place-stayed-open.
